@graph.description: How much does a robotic palletizer cost? See TRF reference list prices, the factors that move the investment and how to estimate payback for your line.

acceptedAnswer.text: A palletizer is a machine that stacks cases, bags, trays or other packed units onto a pallet in a defined pattern at the end of a production line. A robotic palletizer does this with a robot arm and an end-of-arm tool, which makes it flexible across products, SKUs and pallet patterns. TRF Industrial Automation supplies collaborative, compact industrial and high-speed robotic palletizing platforms.

Palletization is the process of arranging packed units into a stable load on a pallet so it can be wrapped, stored, moved by forklift and shipped. It covers the pattern of each layer, the number of layers, the use of slip sheets and how the finished load leaves the line. Robotic palletizing automates that process at the end of the line.

mainEntity.name: How Do I Choose a Palletizing System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose by line speed, case weight and floor space first, then by product type, number of lines and operating environment. Those variables point to a platform, and the end-of-arm tool and pallet pattern are validated per application. Send your line data, and a TRF Sales Engineer confirms which platform fits and what the scope of the quote should include.

mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. These are typical ranges for commercial screening, and TRF confirms the final rate for your product, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach. Applications outside these ranges are engineered as a custom palletizer.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Product?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the case weight plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multi-case picks, the combined weight of the cases. TRFCobot handles cases up to about 22 lb, TRFCompact up to about 44 lb and TRFSpeed up to about 66 lb. Payload also sets the robot class, which is one of the main cost factors of the cell.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Cobot Palletizer and a Traditional Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cobot palletizer uses a collaborative robot, designed for shared workspaces and moderate speeds, in a compact standardized cell with a lower entry cost. A traditional robotic palletizer uses an industrial robot that moves faster, carries heavier loads and runs a higher duty cycle. That is why the TRFCobot Dual has the lowest of the three TRF reference list prices.

mainEntity.name: What Maintenance Does a Robotic Palletizer Require to Avoid Downtime?

acceptedAnswer.text: A robotic palletizer needs periodic inspection of the gripper, sensors and the robot itself, following the manufacturer's schedule, and that yearly cost belongs in your payback estimate. Keep recommended spare parts for wear items on hand. For TRF-supplied equipment, Parts and Service covers technical support, spare parts and the TRFCare preventive maintenance program.
